page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d2c.6xlarge is a big data and storage-focused instance type designed for data-intensive processing and batch workloads. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor, it supplies 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores using hyper-threading on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 88 GB of system memory, delivering approximately 3.67 GB of RAM per vCPU, and is paired with a baseline network bandwidth capacity of 12 Gbps. It does not feature hardware GPU acceleration.

A central component of this instance profile is its bundled 11,918 GB of local HDD storage. This dense physical storage volume delivers high sequential read and write capacity suited for voluminous data sets, albeit with standard mechanical disk latency characteristics compared to solid-state alternatives.

Benchmark data reflects clear performance distinctions between single-threaded execution and multi-threaded throughput. In single-core stress-ng tests, the instance records 1315.48, placing it in the bottom 25% percentile. Single-threaded compression benchmarks similarly fall into lower percentiles, with gzip compression registering 22.63 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 8.65 GB/sec. Conversely, parallel execution scales effectively: multi-core stress-ng reaches 20,953.09 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 93.79 GB/sec, both settling within average benchmark tiers. Large block uncached memory throughput achieves 94.72 GB/sec for reads and 51.67 GB/sec for writes.

From an architectural tradeoff perspective, the ecs.d2c.6xlarge provides high storage density per core at an efficient hardware class profile. It favors high-throughput batch extraction and distributed data pipelines over low-latency single-thread computing. Primary target workloads include Apache Hadoop and Spark processing nodes, large log aggregation pools, data warehousing staging layers, and distributed sequential storage systems.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d2c.6xlarge is a dedicated big data instance featuring 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It includes 88 GB of RAM, a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and a bundled 11,918 GB local HDD storage array without GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations position the instance as a parallel throughput platform: while single-threaded tasks such as single-core stress-ng (1315.48) and single-thread gzip compression (22.63 GB/sec) rank in the lower quartile, multi-threaded metrics perform solidly in the middle range, achieving 20,953.09 in multi-core stress-ng and 93.79 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The massive bundled mechanical disk capacity provides strong density for capacity-driven scenarios, making it well suited for distributed data frameworks, Hadoop or Spark data nodes, log aggregation, and batch sequential data pipelines.
